seo.title: How we work
seo.description: How an Altrazen engagement runs end to end: first conversation, proposal, discovery, build, launch and ongoing support — plus how we handle your code and credentials.

hero.heading: How an engagement actually runs
hero.description: No discovery phase you pay for before knowing whether we are a fit, and no proposal deck. Here is the whole thing, including what we need from you at each point.

timeline.title: First conversation
timeline.description: Thirty to forty-five minutes. You describe what you are building or what is going wrong; we ask what exists today, who depends on it and what the deadline really is. By the end of the call you know whether we are the right people. Sometimes we are not, and we say so.
timeline.whatWeNeed: Half an hour and honest answers. No documents, no preparation.

timeline.title: Proposal and scope
timeline.description: A written proposal: what we will build, what we will not, which engagement model fits, the timeline, and the risks we can already see. If we cannot scope it responsibly without looking at something first, we say that rather than guessing at a number.
timeline.whatWeNeed: A read, and your questions. Push back here — it is much cheaper than pushing back in week six.

timeline.title: Discovery
timeline.description: The short, focused version: users, constraints, integrations, the data model, and what already exists. For a rescue engagement this is the audit instead — read-only access and a written report.
timeline.whatWeNeed: Access to whatever exists, and time with whoever knows the domain best.

timeline.title: Technical plan
timeline.description: Architecture, data model, third-party dependencies and the decisions that would be expensive to reverse, written down with their reasoning. You approve the shape before anyone writes production code.
timeline.whatWeNeed: One review session and a decision.

timeline.title: Build in reviewable slices
timeline.description: Working software on a preview URL every week, arriving as pull requests small enough to actually read. A weekly written update covering what shipped, what is next and anything that changed. No status theatre and no fortnight of silence.
timeline.whatWeNeed: About an hour a week, and answers when a decision is genuinely yours to make.

timeline.title: Harden
timeline.description: Accessibility pass, performance budget, error tracking, backups restored in front of you, and a rollback path you have watched being used. This is part of the build, not a phase that gets cut when the date slips.
timeline.whatWeNeed: Your accounts for hosting, monitoring and any third-party services, so everything lives under your ownership from day one.

timeline.title: Handover, or keep going
timeline.description: Documentation, runbooks and a walkthrough with whoever takes it on. Then either your team runs it, or we do under a maintenance retainer. Both are genuinely fine, and we will tell you which one we think fits your situation.
timeline.whatWeNeed: A decision, and fifteen minutes a month to read the report if we continue.

engagementModels.heading: Three ways to engage
engagementModels.description: We do not publish rates, because a number without a scope is meaningless to both of us. What we can be clear about is the shape of the arrangement. Every proposal names one of these three.

items.name: Fixed-scope project
items.description: A defined outcome, a fixed price and a delivery date, agreed before work starts. Change requests are quoted separately rather than absorbed silently or argued about later.
items.bestFor: A well-understood piece of work: a site, an app, an audit, a stabilisation.
whatYouGet: A price that does not move unless the scope does
A written scope naming what is excluded, not only what is included
Weekly demos against an agreed plan

items.name: Monthly retainer
items.description: A recurring block of engineering time each month for maintenance, small changes and improvements. Rolling, cancellable with thirty days' notice, and it always ends with a handover document.
items.bestFor: Software that is live and needs to stay patched, monitored and gently improved.
whatYouGet: A named engineer who knows your codebase rather than a ticket queue
Security patching, dependency upgrades and verified backups on a schedule
Monitoring answered by us before you notice
A written monthly report you can forward to anyone

items.name: Dedicated team
items.description: One or more engineers working only on your product for an agreed period, planning with you week to week. Effectively your engineering team, without the hiring cycle.
items.bestFor: Ongoing product development where the roadmap will change as you learn.
whatYouGet: Consistent people who build context rather than rotating staff
Weekly planning and a shared backlog you control
Direct access to the engineers, with no account manager relaying
The ability to change direction without renegotiating a contract

security.heading: What happens to your code
security.description: This is the question everyone has and most people are too polite to ask, so here is the answer in public.

items.title: Mutual NDA first
items.description: Signed before you grant any access at all. It covers your code, your data, your business model and anything we happen to see along the way.

items.title: The narrowest access that works
items.description: An audit needs to read your code, not change it, so it gets read-only. Write access exists only where the work requires it, only on a working branch, and only after you have agreed to it.

items.title: Credentials in an encrypted manager
items.description: Anything you send us goes into an encrypted password manager. Never email, never chat, never a shared document. We ask you to revoke our access when the engagement ends.

items.title: No subcontractors
items.description: Only the people working on your engagement see your repository. We do not pass your code to a third party or an outsourced team.

items.title: Your accounts, from day one
items.description: Hosting, domains, app store listings, monitoring and third-party services are set up under your ownership, not ours. Nothing about leaving us is difficult by design.

items.title: Findings stay private
items.description: We do not discuss what we found in your codebase with anyone. Anything that ever appears in a public case study is anonymised and shown to you for approval first. If you say no, it does not go up.

cta.heading: Start at week zero
cta.description: Thirty minutes, no preparation needed. We will tell you honestly whether we are the right people for it.
